headline: Indian stock markets drop as FII outflows, elevated crude oil prices, and global rate hikes trigger weakness

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Persistent foreign institutional investor (FII) outflows created downward pressure on equity markets.
Surging crude oil prices and global rate hike concerns heightened risk aversion among investors.
Weak global cues and volatile market sentiment led to a loss of intraday gains.
whatHappening: Nifty fell 96 points while the Sensex slipped to 72,480 amid market volatility.
Indian benchmark indices logged their worst monthly performance since March as September concluded.
The Cabinet approved a ₹1.86 trillion green energy corridor scheme with battery storage.
Tax authorities flagged alleged fake e-waste claims involving select consumer electronics manufacturers.
summary: Indian equities closed September on a weak note as rising crude oil prices and heavy FII selling dragged key indices down. Market volatility prevented Sensex and Nifty from maintaining intraday recovery attempts. Key policy highlights included Cabinet approval for a ₹1.86 trillion green energy corridor scheme and ongoing SEBI-RBI efforts to ease FPI onboarding.
